Aisha Khan: Quick heads-up — launching a pilot called the Return Buddy Program for teammates returning from longer leaves (8+ weeks) :seedling:
Aisha Khan: TL;DR: one peer buddy for up to 4 weeks, weekly buddy check-ins, optional manager 1:1s, and a small $200 buddy honorarium. Purpose: reduce cognitive load, clarify ramp priorities, and catch regressions early. :tada:
Aisha Khan: Who's eligible: full-time and part-time employees returning from parental, caregiver, or medical leave. Contractors are not eligible for the stipend but can participate informally — see below.
Aisha Khan: How it works:
- People Ops assigns a buddy (same org / similar role). Buddy commits ~2–4 hrs/week for 4 weeks.
- Manager runs a quick 30-min return sync in week 1 and an alignment check in week 3.
- Buddy completes a short checklist (ramp goals, critical systems, active projects) and flags blockers to manager/People Ops.
Aisha Khan: Sign-up / nominations: manager or returning employee fills this form: https://forms.redwood.ai/return-buddy (form id: RB-2026)
Aisha Khan: If you'd like to be a buddy, indicate availability on the form. People Ops will honor volunteer preferences where possible.
Nate Rivera: Are international teammates eligible for the $200 honorarium?
Aisha Khan: Good q — yes, it's global. We'll issue the honorarium via payroll where possible; if payroll country rules block it we'll offer an alternate (gift card or training credit). People Ops will reach out case-by-case.
Samir Patel: What about contractors? I might want to be a buddy for someone returning who’s a contractor.
Aisha Khan: Contractors can absolutely be buddies informally, but the stipend is for Redwood payroll employees only. We'll note contractor participation on the form so managers can factor it into load planning.
Elena Gomez: Can we add a short micro-onboarding checklist to the Console onboarding flow so returning folks have a single place for links?
Aisha Khan: Yes — planning to add a "Return checklist" doc to the People Ops wiki and a short card in Console. ETA: 2 weeks.
Jonas Li: Please also add an item to the hiring manager guide about pausing role handoffs during the first 2 weeks after return — avoided churn last time.
Aisha Khan: Great call, Jonas. We'll add that.
hr-bot: Form RB-2026 received 1 new submission (auto): returning_employee=Elena Gomez, expected_return=2026-07-05.
Aisha Khan: Roadmap for pilot: run for 3 months, collect quick pulse survey at week 2 and week 6, evaluate participation and rollout to all teams.
Aisha Khan: Quick policy notes — this program complements existing PTO/leave policies (no changes to leave entitlements). If you need extended flexibility (>4 weeks), talk to your manager + People Ops for an accommodation plan.
Samir Patel: Awesome initiative. Will managers get an email with suggested 30-min sync agenda?
Aisha Khan: Yep — agenda template & buddy checklist will be in the wiki and we'll ping managers automatically when a form is submitted.
Elena Gomez: Happy to volunteer as a buddy this quarter. Please put me down as "frontend" and "EM cadence" preferences on the form.
Aisha Khan: Thank you! :heart:
Nate Rivera: How will we measure success?
Aisha Khan: Good metric ideas: ramp time to PR authoring, number of blocker escalations, and self-reported confidence from returning teammates. We'll share results after the pilot.
Aisha Khan: If anyone wants to discuss edge cases (extended international leave, phased returns, ADA accommodations), DM People Ops or drop them on the form comment field.
Aisha Khan: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick feedback. We'll update the wiki once the pilot assets are live.
